title: substrate = cloud: tk cloud spawn/wait/collect/reconcile for local orchestrators
description:
D19: the cloud substrate must be drivable by ANY orchestrator location, not only the Workflow-hosted one. Expose the run API as the tk cloud verb family mirroring tk herd: spawn, wait, collect, reconcile. A local Claude Code, omp or Pi session sets substrate = "cloud" in runners.toml and drives worker containers from the laptop — local judgement, cloud hands.

Consequences to implement, not just document:
- Five parallel implementers stop costing local worktrees, CPU or battery.
- A lid closed mid-wave loses only the orchestrator, which is the failure every runner already recovers from.
- ONE LEASE wherever the orchestrator sits: on an enrolled project a LOCAL run takes the same RunRoom lease as a cloud run, or a laptop session and a scheduled run collide on .tick/. Un-enrolled projects keep the local file lease; enrolment upgrades the arbiter and never installs a second one.
- The degenerate case stays sacred: a fully local orchestrator on the harness or herdr substrate with no cloud enrolment keeps working offline, forever.
acceptance_criteria: A local orchestrator with substrate = cloud runs a wave in cloud containers and integrates it; the same run refuses when a cloud run holds the lease, naming the holder; a project with no cloud enrolment still runs fully offline on the herdr substrate.
